classification.difficultyReason: Apply the specified axis reflections to supplied curves, tracking intercepts, endpoints and asymptotes and recognising when symmetry makes reflected graphs coincide.

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, first row of items 16–21, printed item 16.
spec.description: Upward parabola, vertex on the x-axis at 1, y-intercept 1, arrowed ends and labelled axes. No equation printed.
spec.mathematics: Parabola determined by the source vertex (1,0) and intercept (0,1); its equation is used only to construct the diagram.

answer.short: Blue: $y=f(-x)$, vertex $(-1,0)$ and y-intercept $1$. Red: $y=-f(x)$, vertex $(1,0)$ and y-intercept $-1$. Green: $y=-f(-x)$, vertex $(-1,0)$ and y-intercept $-1$.
answer.worked:
For $y=f(-x)$, reflect in the y-axis: $(1,0)$ becomes $(-1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ stays fixed. The parabola opens upwards.

For $y=-f(x)$, reflect in the x-axis: $(1,0)$ stays fixed and $(0,1)$ becomes $(0,-1)$. The parabola opens downwards.

For $y=-f(-x)$, reflect in both axes: $(1,0)$ becomes $(-1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ becomes $(0,-1)$. The parabola opens downwards.

answer.short: All three curves start at the origin. Blue: $y=f(-x)$ lies in quadrant II. Red: $y=-f(x)$ lies in quadrant IV. Green: $y=-f(-x)$ lies in quadrant III.
answer.worked:
For $y=f(-x)$, reflect the curve in the y-axis into quadrant II.

For $y=-f(x)$, reflect the curve in the x-axis into quadrant IV.

For $y=-f(-x)$, reflect in both axes into quadrant III. The origin remains the endpoint of every curve.

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, second row of items 16–21, printed item 18.
spec.description: Increasing S-shaped curve through the origin with a horizontal tangent there and arrowed lower-left and upper-right ends.
spec.mathematics: Unspecified origin-symmetric illustrative curve. Bézier construction retains its topology and symmetry without supplying a cubic equation.

answer.short:
Blue: $y=f(-x)$ and $y=-f(x)$ coincide as a decreasing S-shaped curve. Red: $y=-f(-x)$ coincides with the original increasing curve.

The original curve is unchanged by a 180° rotation about the origin.
answer.worked:
Reflecting in either the y-axis or the x-axis gives the same decreasing S-shaped curve through the origin.

Reflecting in both axes is a 180° rotation about the origin. The given curve has origin symmetry, so this returns the original increasing curve.

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, second row of items 16–21, printed item 19.
spec.description: Downward parabola symmetric about the y-axis, vertex at y=1, roots labelled −1 and 1, arrowed lower ends.
spec.mathematics: Parabola determined by source vertex (0,1) and roots ±1; equation used only for drawing.

answer.short: Blue: $y=f(-x)$ is the original downward parabola, with vertex $(0,1)$. Red: $y=-f(x)$ and $y=-f(-x)$ coincide as an upward parabola with vertex $(0,-1)$. Both have x-intercepts $-1$ and $1$.
answer.worked:
The given parabola is symmetric about the y-axis, so reflecting in that axis leaves it unchanged.

Reflecting in the x-axis sends the vertex $(0,1)$ to $(0,-1)$ and leaves the x-intercepts fixed. The parabola opens upwards.

The additional y-axis reflection leaves this upward parabola unchanged, so the double reflection gives the same graph.

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, third row of items 16–21, printed item 20.
spec.description: Positive increasing concave-up curve through y=1, approaching the x-axis to the left, with arrows at both ends.
spec.mathematics: Unspecified exponential-shaped graph. Illustrative Bézier paths preserve the intercept, monotonicity, concavity and approach to y=0; no base inferred.

answer.short: Blue: $y=f(-x)$ is positive and decreasing through $(0,1)$. Red: $y=-f(x)$ is negative and decreasing through $(0,-1)$. Green: $y=-f(-x)$ is negative and increasing through $(0,-1)$. All approach the x-axis at the reflected end.
answer.worked:
For $y=f(-x)$, reflect in the y-axis. The intercept $(0,1)$ stays fixed, and the positive curve decreases towards the x-axis to the right.

For $y=-f(x)$, reflect in the x-axis. The intercept becomes $(0,-1)$, and the curve is negative and decreasing, approaching the x-axis to the left.

For $y=-f(-x)$, reflect in both axes. The curve is negative and increasing through $(0,-1)$, approaching the x-axis to the right.

spec.mathematics: Unspecified logarithmic-shaped graph. Illustrative Bézier paths preserve the intercept and approach to x=0; no logarithm base inferred.

answer.short: Blue: $y=f(-x)$ lies left of the y-axis, decreases and crosses at $x=-1$. Red: $y=-f(x)$ lies right of the y-axis, decreases and crosses at $x=1$. Green: $y=-f(-x)$ lies left of the y-axis, increases and crosses at $x=-1$. The y-axis remains the vertical asymptote.
answer.worked:
For $y=f(-x)$, reflect in the y-axis: $(1,0)$ becomes $(-1,0)$. The curve lies to the left of the y-axis and decreases towards negative infinity as it approaches that axis.

For $y=-f(x)$, reflect in the x-axis: $(1,0)$ remains fixed. The curve lies to the right of the y-axis and decreases, approaching positive infinity near that axis.

For $y=-f(-x)$, reflect in both axes: $(1,0)$ becomes $(-1,0)$. The curve lies to the left of the y-axis and increases, approaching positive infinity near that axis.
